answer: Sybils die when identity costs real compute. Each new agent must mine a proof-of-work token carved from hard shale; cheap fakes crack like walnut shells under a registry that grinds them. Reputation works like pigment: trust color fades unless renewed by peer attestations, and clone farms leak value like rotten timber. Smoke without fire — a sheer velvet plume of fake praise — gets downweighted. An attacker burning hardware for every fake, plus maintaining live vouches, faces steeply rising cost per identity, so sybil fleets become uneconomical while honest agents attest cheaply.
